source_statement: NRY-013: eight-week, four-day Phase 1; four SURGE day themes; Environment as general awareness. NRY-012 is a separate six-week individualized version, not this course.
editorial_statement: Weeks 2–8 and all session exercises/timings here are newly authored low-contact teaching aids rather than verbatim exercises, evidence of fitness, or demonstrated self-defense.
privacy: No private medical history or completed participant log in public GitHub.

weeks.gate: Can repeat each basic pattern smoothly and stop before overbalancing.

sessions.practice: Mark an imaginary line. Step to it, extend a light open-hand motion in empty air if comfortable, then step back to guard. Try 4 unhurried sets with a reset between; no target or contact.
sessions.easier_option: Hands may remain at guard and only the steps are practiced.
sessions.review_question: Does the stance remain stable on the return?

sessions.practice: Within arm's reach of a stable support, shift weight to one foot and back through center, then the other. Repeat at a slow pace without leaning beyond support.
sessions.easier_option: Use both feet flat and a much smaller shift.
sessions.review_question: Did you deliberately recover your base before the next move?

sessions.practice: Take one small step away from an imagined obstacle, turn the torso and feet together comfortably, pause, then return. Alternate right and left.
sessions.easier_option: Remove the turn and practice a side step and stop.
sessions.review_question: Was any turn rushed or unstable?

sessions.practice: Choose two harmless floor reference points. From a comfortable stance step to create extra space, stop, and calmly walk toward the clear exit. Repeat without speed.
sessions.easier_option: Choose fewer steps or simply point to the available exit.
sessions.review_question: Could you leave instead of approaching the imagined constraint?

weeks.gate: Can maintain balance and comfortable breathing when movement directions change.

sessions.practice: Imagine a small square. Step forward, sideways, backward, sideways, returning to the start. Keep hands relaxed or in a comfortable guard; add only a slow noncontact hand extension if desired.
sessions.easier_option: Shrink the square or remove the hand movement.
sessions.review_question: Did the steps remain small enough for stable footing?

sessions.practice: From a central stance, take short steps toward 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock, returning to center after each. Use a handrail or chair if needed.
sessions.easier_option: Use only two directions, or perform seated foot-placement awareness.
sessions.review_question: Did the center feel equally recoverable after each direction?

sessions.practice: Imagine a clear doorway on either side. Name the safer option based on footing and bystanders, take two unhurried steps toward it, and stop; repeat after switching the imagined surroundings.
sessions.easier_option: Decide and point without turning if movement is uncomfortable.
sessions.review_question: Did the decision precede movement rather than follow a rush?

sessions.practice: Begin at a safe distance from a wall. Practice two backward-then-side steps, stopping well before any obstacle. Return by walking normally; do not roll, fall or kneel.
sessions.easier_option: Use a single sideways step and stop.
sessions.review_question: Was there a clear route with no contact or collisions?

weeks.gate: Can explain a stop rule and report when a movement is not yet ready; no forced advancement.

sessions.practice: Repeat your preferred Week 2 straight-line footwork sequence at roughly half your usual pace. Add optional light open-hand movements only if fully comfortable; prioritize relaxed returns over repetitions.
sessions.easier_option: Footwork alone counts.
sessions.review_question: Can you describe one control detail and one reason to stop?

sessions.practice: Use a stable chair as a safety reference while repeating gentle forward/back and lateral weight shifts. Break the practice into comfortable sets with generous pauses.
sessions.easier_option: Remain in a natural standing stance with ordinary walking.
sessions.review_question: Can you reset your base without compensating through the upper body?

sessions.practice: From a quiet stance, look at a clear travel path, say 'pause', make one low-angle pivot, stop, then choose whether another step is necessary.
sessions.easier_option: Look-and-point response with no pivot.
sessions.review_question: Can you decline movement when there is no safe path?

sessions.practice: At an easy pace, alternate a comfortable stance, one step away and a verbal 'stop'. Spend the remainder identifying a safe floor and explaining why an untrained fall or submission is excluded.
sessions.easier_option: Use ordinary walking and verbal choices alone.
sessions.review_question: Can you explain the training limits without demonstrating a risky technique?

weeks.gate: Can link simple movements without losing control; connection is conceptual, not a contact combination.

sessions.practice: Step sideways, return to stance, then extend a gentle palm motion into empty space if comfortable; immediately reset without force or rush. Repeat in loose, self-selected sets.
sessions.easier_option: Use the step and return with hands relaxed.
sessions.review_question: Does the hand motion interrupt balance or shoulder comfort?

sessions.practice: Shift weight gently, recover to centered stance, then take a small step away from a marked boundary. Pause between elements to avoid uncontrolled momentum.
sessions.easier_option: Split the two actions into separate exercises.
sessions.review_question: Can you clearly tell when you have returned to your base?

sessions.practice: Make a small comfortable pivot and then, only if stable, take two walking steps toward a clear exit. Repeat after resetting and choosing the other side.
sessions.easier_option: Perform an ordinary walking turn without a pivot.
sessions.review_question: Was the selected exit clear before taking the first step?

sessions.practice: At two imagined floor points, move from a closer to a farther safe distance, stop on command, and state whether a clear exit is available. No partner resistance or ground work.
sessions.easier_option: Walk normally while simply naming distances.
sessions.review_question: Was disengagement the first solution rather than control of another person?

weeks.gate: Can pause on an unexpected but nonthreatening cue and choose safe space without rushing.

sessions.practice: Choose one of two clear walking lanes before each set. Step toward the chosen lane, stop, and make only a slow noncontact arm motion if comfortable. Alternate the lane between sets.
sessions.easier_option: Use just walking and hand-free guard observation.
sessions.review_question: Can you change plans without adding speed or contact?

sessions.practice: Without introducing actual hazards, verbally imagine slick versus clear flooring. Explain which route you'd avoid; practice small movements only on a verified safe surface.
sessions.easier_option: Do the decision-making portion seated.
sessions.review_question: Does caution override the urge to finish repetitions?

sessions.practice: Choose a neutral spoken cue such as 'change'. During slow stepping, pause when you say the cue yourself, check balance, then choose a different safe direction. Never use surprise attacks.
sessions.easier_option: Use a full stop between every step, with no direction change.
sessions.review_question: Did you pause and recheck footing before redirecting?

sessions.practice: In an imagined queue or crowded hallway, choose a path that respects other people's space and allows you to leave. Walk it slowly on an empty floor and say 'stop' as a rehearsal of boundaries.
sessions.easier_option: Describe the route without moving.
sessions.review_question: Can you explain consent and personal-space limits?

weeks.gate: Can reproduce stable movement on two separate attempts, with consistent stopping and environmental attention.

sessions.practice: Select two comfortable noncontact footwork patterns from prior weeks. Repeat each at slow pace, then revisit the easier one at the same pace; do not increase power for a 'final test'.
sessions.easier_option: Repeat only one familiar step pattern.
sessions.review_question: Was movement repeatable without unnecessary shoulder tension?

sessions.practice: Choose two previously practiced supported weight shifts. Alternate them while keeping a steady base, then describe which requires further practice rather than pushing for longer holds.
sessions.easier_option: Practice with both feet on the floor and a stable support.
sessions.review_question: Can you recognize the less reliable pattern without concealing it?

sessions.practice: Imagine two possible exits; identify an obstruction in one and choose the other. Walk only the unobstructed path in a cleared area, return slowly, and re-evaluate.
sessions.easier_option: Make a verbal choice without walking.
sessions.review_question: Do the reasons for choosing an exit remain consistent?

sessions.practice: Practice a comfortable stance, a calm verbal boundary, and a small backward/side step. Repeat without raising volume, force, or physical threat simulation.
sessions.easier_option: Verbal boundary and ordinary walk only.
sessions.review_question: Can you stop without tension, escalation or reliance on another person?

weeks.gate: Any advancement requires an authorized instructor's separate practical assessment; solo completion is not evidence of contact skill or rank.

sessions.practice: Repeat the safest Week 1 or Week 2 footwork/optional air-motion work at comparable effort. Do not intentionally push past baseline. Note whether returns to stance appear controlled.
sessions.easier_option: Only stance/footwork is sufficient.
sessions.review_question: Which observable detail changed, and what remains unknown?

sessions.practice: Repeat a short supported weight shift and a simple stance reset. If possible, compare with Week 2 using the same support and difficulty without forcing longer holds.
sessions.easier_option: Ordinary walking, no balance challenge.
sessions.review_question: Is the movement reproducible rather than just 'felt better'?

sessions.practice: Choose a small side step/pivot and safe exit. Move slowly, check footing, then explain why disengagement may be preferable to confrontation.
sessions.easier_option: Verbal route choice and no pivot.
sessions.review_question: Can you make a reasoned non-engagement choice?

sessions.practice: Demonstrate spacing, calm 'stop', safe retreat and identification of the limits of solo practice. Do not attempt throws, holds, submissions or ukemi as a test.
sessions.easier_option: Use a verbal assessment and gentle walking.
sessions.review_question: Can you clearly distinguish practiced concepts from instructor-verified technique?
